heroHeadline: Bamako Siege Day 19: WFP Suspends Operations, Food Prices Double; RTB Confirms Djibo Scale; Goïta Granted 5-Year Term as Parties Dissolved
heroSubtitle: On May 16–17, Burkina Faso's state broadcaster RTB officially confirmed 'hundreds or thousands' of JNIM fighters assaulted Djibo on May 11 — the first government acknowledgment of the attack's full scale, five days after the assault. The International Crisis Group simultaneously published a major analysis titled 'Major Jihadist Attack Exposes Military Failings in Burkina Faso,' documenting how a FAB fighter jet turned back under JNIM fire, armed drones were not deployed, and helicopter reinforcements arrived only after JNIM voluntarily withdrew. In Mali, the World Food Programme suspended all field operations in central Mali as Bamako's siege enters Day 19: 3 of 6 main entry roads remain disrupted, the Manantali power grid is under degraded capacity, and food prices have doubled since April 28. A government-organized national dialogue in Bamako granted junta leader Goïta a five-year presidential term and formally dissolved all remaining political parties by decree — completing Mali's transition to permanent authoritarian governance amid the worst security crisis since 2012.
